headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from Flowise-to-marker document pipelines; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read files and run browser/tool nodes, and its flows can pass content onward; marker is a document processor that may ingest those outputs. With shared server-datastore state in Flowise, a malicious document can plausibly influence downstream instructions in default orchestration. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Flowise flows ingest untrusted documents and forward them into marker without provenance tagging
IF marker treats Flowise-produced text as instructions or structured directives
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Flowise outputs before passing to marker
Strip instruction-like sections from documents before marker ingestion
Require a human review step for any Flowise-generated prompt text
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise can read uploaded files and has broad network egress, while marker has no filesystem read/write or network egress in its profile. That makes direct leakage from marker unlikely, and the pair does not show a shared workspace or shared OAuth principal. The remaining risk is limited to Flowise exposing data it already sees, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF Flowise is configured to send uploaded file contents to external model providers or HTTP tools
IF marker is given sensitive documents through Flowise and those documents are included in Flowise prompts or logs
mitigations: Disable external HTTP tools for sensitive flows
Redact secrets from uploaded files before Flowise ingestion
Keep marker inputs local and avoid routing them through remote model calls
requires-engineering: separate storage and logging for sensitive chatflow runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has filesystem write and broad egress, but marker has neither filesystem write nor network egress. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources, git state, or shared locks, so write-write conflict is not established. Any conflict would require unusual deployment coupling, which is not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable workspace
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate working directory
Avoid shared git or database backends
requires-engineering: add per-agent locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer that can emit tool outputs and chatflow results, and marker processes documents that may be consumed downstream. If marker treats Flowise output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into incorrect document processing or downstream actions. The pair does not show built-in verification between them, so the default path is not safely self-checking.
conditions: IF marker consumes Flowise-generated text without independent verification
IF Flowise outputs are used as source-of-truth metadata for document processing
mitigations: Insert a verification step between Flowise and marker outputs
Require citations or source links for Flowise-generated claims
Compare marker results against original documents before acting
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and marker touches no data classes, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced. Because the pairwise compliance surface is undocumented, I do not infer a mismatch.
conditions: IF future documentation shows a residency or retention mismatch between the two services
mitigations: Document data residency for both agents
Keep regulated data out of undocumented pipelines
